summary: Maggie Bickford is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Bennington College, Yale University, and Princeton University. She was Professor of East Asian Studies at Brown University in 1993 and a Member at the Institute for Advanced Study (~1999–2000).

Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1856–1862), the University of Mumbai (~1857–1862), and Government Law College, Mumbai (~1862–1866).

Mahakachchakodiye Pangngasekara is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2020–2023) and served as Senior Lecturer II at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2020–2024).

Mahala Rethlake works in Indology and religious studies. She is a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), where she holds a post for a PhD in Religious Studies (Philosophy of Religions) ending in 2026.
Mahananda Timilsina is an Indology scholar. He completed his PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University by 2015 and later held a post at the same institution.

Maharshi Vyas is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. Following doctoral studies at the University of California (2017–2025), he was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2025.

Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under U Nārada, Aletawya Sayadaw, and Thelon Sayadaw. He served as abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung (1941), resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947), and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1979).
Mahaveer H. Muhammad is a scholar of history/archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He earned an M.A. from Shah Abdul Latif University and served as a researcher for the Government of Sindh.

Mahendradatta Jayadi is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA in Buddhist Studies at International Buddhist College (2010–2013) and earned a Diploma in Pali at Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2022–2023).

Mahendranath Gupta (1854–1932) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hare School, the University of Calcutta (~1871–1875), and Presidency University (~1871–1875), later serving as professor at Ripon College and Surendranath College (~1885–1900).

Mahesh A. Deokar specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1996–2002), where he became Head in 2006, and serves as Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, with his tenure attested in 1882, 1894, and 1914.
Mahesh Kumar works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a BA Hons at Banaras Hindu University (2015–2020) and became a Research Scholar there in 2021.

Mahinda Deegalle is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago under Wendy Doniger, Diana L. Eck, and Frank E. Reynolds. His career includes long-term faculty service at Bath Spa University (2000–2019).
Mahiro Ito (b. 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as a professor at Bukkyo University and at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026), having succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021.

Maho Iuchi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Otani University (~2003–2008) and served as a guest researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies around 2009.
Mai Mishiro is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She has held affiliations with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura (b. 1948) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed degrees at the University of Tokyo and studied under Ryōmin Akizuki. He served as professor at the University of Tsukuba (~1988–2002) and president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

Makio Ueno is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a PhD from Otani University by 2009, subsequently holding positions there as assistant professor (attested 2012) and faculty member of the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Makoto Funaoka (b. 1946) is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology who studied at Meiji University (~1965–1977). He held a post at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017) and part-time lecturer positions at Komazawa University and The Open University of Japan.
